note: The alignment pictures' cameras and moments (render/alignments.py). Where a camera stands, its lens and the exposure are look choices; every sky is one of build/sky-bake.json's (`pnpm run sky-bake`): a night of `nights`, or a sky of `alignments.skies`. Camera `at` is metres in the project frame (+x east, +y north, +z up from Khufu's base); `az` is degrees from north through east and `pitch` degrees above level; `shift` is Blender's lens shift.

c4-night.why: A drone's view from 1.3 km north of Khufu and 150 m up, looking south along the meridian, level with the frame shifted up so the pyramids stand straight: the whole of Orion on the horizon over the three pyramids on the night of 10,450 BCE, Alnitak on the meridian.

moment.label: mid-morning at the equinox, the pyramids' shadows thrown north-west

c4-plan.why: The plateau from straight above, north up, for laying the belt on the ground.

c5-dawn-10500.why: Close behind and above the lion, 12 m north of its axis so its head stands clear of the sun, looking due east along its gaze at the equinox dawn of 10,500 BCE. The stars are brightened 25-fold (star_gain) so they show against the twilight as the eye sees them; the dome is tuned for a dark night.

c5-dawn-2500.why: The same place and the same moment of the equinox dawn, 2500 BCE, the Sphinx as Khafre's people recut it.

c2-xray-2450.why: The Great Pyramid from due east, level, so the north-south plane its shafts lie in faces the camera and every slope reads true; high enough to see the Queen's Chamber over the queens' pyramids.

c2-xray-10450.why: The same, under the sky of 10,450 BCE.

portholes.note: One per shaft and epoch, generated from the bake's C2 section: a camera out along the shaft's line looking up it, the zenith up, under the sky of the star that crossed the line. The lens gives a 30 degree field on a square frame.
